prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_E:
Summary of key proposals and commitments (within 500 words)

Core five pledges
- Cut class sizes for 5–7 year-olds to 30 or under by ending the assisted places scheme.
- Halve the time from arrest to sentencing for persistent young offenders.
- Cut NHS waiting lists by treating an extra 100,000 patients using £100m saved from bureaucracy.
- Get 250,000 under-25s off benefit and into work via a windfall levy on privatised utilities.
- No rise in basic or top income tax rates; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%; aim for low inflation and interest rates.

Education
- Make education the top priority; raise its share of national income over a Parliament as spending on social/economic failure falls.
- Guaranteed nursery places for all four year-olds; targets toward universal provision for three year-olds.
- Reduce infant class sizes; focus on literacy/numeracy with clear targets, phonics, and whole-class maths teaching; baseline assessment and annual improvement targets.
- “Fresh start” for failing schools; education action zones; more parental involvement and homework guidelines.
- Expand IT access: wire up schools and create a National Grid for Learning; train teachers in IT using lottery funds.
- Strengthen teaching: induction year, General Teaching Council, fast removal of incompetent teachers; mandatory headship qualification.
- Higher education: income-related graduate repayments; expand lifelong learning, Individual Learning Accounts, and a University for Industry.

Economy, tax, and spending
- Maintain 2.5% or lower inflation target; reform the Bank of England for more effective, accountable monetary policy.
- Fiscal rules: borrow only to invest over the cycle; keep debt at prudent levels; adhere to existing spending limits for two years.
- No increases in basic/top income tax; long-term aim for a 10p starting rate; retain zero VAT on essentials; cut VAT on fuel to 5%.
- Promote saving/investment (new ISAs; review corporate/CGT); central spending review to shift resources to priorities.

Jobs, business, and work
- Welfare-to-work: four options for under-25s (private jobs with rebates, voluntary sector jobs, education/training, environment taskforce); rebates to hire long-term unemployed; support for lone parents back to work; tackle benefit fraud.
- Tougher competition law; balanced, predictable utility regulation.
- Reinvigorate public–private partnerships and infrastructure; support SMEs (cut late payment, reduce red tape, improve Business Links).
- Regional Development Agencies; strengthen science/technology links; promote green technologies; expand renewables and CHP; no case for new nuclear stations.
- Sensibly set national minimum wage via an independent low pay commission; union recognition where a workforce votes for it; retain key balloting and picketing rules; support EU Social Chapter focused on employability.

NHS and public health
- End the internal market; primary care-led commissioning; 3–5 year service agreements; measure outcomes not “episodes.”
- Annual real-terms funding increases directed to patient care; eliminate mixed-sex wards over time.
- Ban tobacco advertising; create an independent Food Standards Agency; promote telemedicine; improve PFI delivery.

Crime and justice
- Fast-track youth justice; single final warning; Youth Offender Teams; parental responsibility orders.
- Decentralise and streamline prosecution; clearer sentencing guidelines; reduce police bureaucracy; tackle antisocial behaviour; new offences for racial harassment/racially motivated violence.
- Anti-drugs coordinator; pilot compulsory testing/treatment orders; strengthen victim support.
- Free vote on a complete ban on handguns.

Families, housing, and older people
- National childcare strategy; support for reasonable limits on working hours, holidays, and unpaid parental leave; retain universal Child Benefit uprated with prices.
- Protect homeowners (flexible mortgages, anti-gazumping); invest council house sale receipts in new and refurbished social housing; license HMOs; introduce commonhold; restore duties toward the homeless.
- Retain and uprate the basic state pension; promote stakeholder and occupational pensions; retain SERPS option; stronger consumer protection and pension-splitting on divorce; Royal Commission on long-term care; independent inspection of care.

Environment, transport, culture, and sport
- Make all departments responsible for environmental goals; establish an environmental audit committee.
- Integrated transport: stronger rail regulation and a new rail authority; public/private partnership for London Underground; safer roads, bus partnerships, cleaner vehicles, strategic roads review.
- Rural services protection; CAP reform; responsible countryside access; wildlife and animal welfare measures.
- Create NESTA to back young talent; reform lottery distribution and seek a not-for-profit operator at contract renewal; protect school playing fields; support hosting major sporting events.

Constitutional and citizens’ rights
- End voting rights of hereditary peers; review appointments; modernise Commons procedures; transparent party funding and ban foreign donations.
- Freedom of Information Act; incorporate the European Convention on Human Rights into UK law; strengthen civil rights for disabled people; legal aid reform.
- Devolution subject to referendums: a Scottish parliament with limited tax powers; a Welsh assembly with secondary powers; London mayor and strategic authority; regional chambers and possible elected assemblies by regional consent; strengthen local government performance and accountability.
- Fairer, faster immigration/asylum decisions; streamline appeals; regulate advisers; address backlogs.

Northern Ireland
- Support the peace process, human rights, policing confidence, anti-discrimination, and economic development; combat terrorism.

Europe, defence, and foreign policy
- Lead EU reforms: complete the single market, enlarge to Central/Eastern Europe and Cyprus, reform CAP/CFP, increase institutional openness, retain vetoes on key national interests, consider limited QMV where beneficial; sign the Social Chapter.
- Single currency: decision by Cabinet, Parliament, and a referendum; based on national interest and genuine convergence.
- Defence based on NATO; strategic defence and security review; retain Trident while pursuing multilateral nuclear reductions; ban anti-personnel landmines; tighten arms export controls; defence diversification.
- UN reform; elevate international development with a dedicated department; reverse the decline in aid and reaffirm the 0.7% target; debt relief and fair trade; consider rejoining UNESCO.
- Make human rights central, support an international criminal court; target a 20% CO2 reduction by 2010 and lead on global climate agreements.

TEXT_D:
Summary of the 1997 manifesto (policy-focused, non-ideological)

Education and skills
- Invest £2bn per year (funded by +1p on basic income tax).
- Universal high‑quality early years places for 3–4 year‑olds; scrap vouchers.
- Double schools’ books/equipment in year one; reduce primary classes to max 30 within 5 years; £500m over 5 years for repairs.
- General Teaching Council; literacy drive; replace National Curriculum with a Minimum Curriculum Entitlement; strengthen inspection and discipline policies; full funding for Special Educational Needs.
- Devolve more powers to schools; integrate grant‑maintained/CTCs; decisions on selection left to local communities.
- Phase out Assisted Places; encourage state‑independent partnerships.
- Individual Learning Accounts; income‑linked student repayments; oppose top‑up fees; credit‑based system post‑14.
- 2% remissible training levy (SMEs exempt); ensure all 16–19s get at least two days/week education or training; Quality Council for post‑16; connect schools to the internet.

Economy, enterprise and consumers
- Operational independence for the central bank to target low inflation; fiscal “golden rule”; distinguish capital/current spending; expand PPPs.
- Support entry to a single European currency if criteria met and backed by referendum.
- “Working benefits” to incentivise hiring the long‑term unemployed; encourage saving via new schemes.
- Support SMEs: late‑payment interest right; less red tape; improve finance access; reform local business rates long‑term; favour SMEs in procurement.
- Regional Development Agencies; boost R&D (shift from military to civil); tech transfer centres.
- Stronger competition law; merge OFT/MMC; overhaul utility regulation into a single consumer‑focused office; enhance financial services regulation and redress.

Environment, energy and transport
- Embed environmental goals across government; new department for environment/energy; stronger Environment Agency.
- Targets including cutting CO2 by 30% from 1990 levels within 15 years.
- Tax shift from jobs/VAT towards pollution (phased carbon tax); cut VAT on energy‑saving materials.
- National home insulation programme prioritising low‑income households.
- Promote renewables; no subsidies for nuclear; no replacements at end of life; shift nuclear funds to decommissioning/waste.
- Invest in public transport; allow urban road pricing to fund transit; keep London Underground public with access to private finance.
- Rail: treble freight and double passengers by 2010; enforce Railtrack investment/traffic targets, with power to reacquire a controlling interest if persistent failure.
- Cut annual car tax for small cars, offset by gradual fuel duty rise; greener company car regime; planning reform to reduce travel.
- Water: leakage targets; fairer charging; share excess profits with customers; end damaging discharges within 10 years.
- Animal welfare: national commission; tighter EU transport limits; bans on testing for cosmetics/weapons/tobacco; stronger protections for wild species; free vote on hunting.

Housing, crime and communities
- Build more affordable homes via public/private/housing association partnerships; release council capital receipts; new Mortgage Benefit for first‑time buyers (existing MIR protected).
- End rough sleeping by 2000 with rent deposit schemes and more hostels; tenant repair rights; empty homes strategy; scrap shared‑residency rule for housing benefit.
- 3,000 more police within a year; cut paperwork; expand restorative justice; overhaul CPS; crime‑prevention partnerships; Royal Commission on drugs; stronger victim support; improve police accountability and action on racial/homophobic violence.
- Rural: reform CAP to management contracts; diversify economies; bolster rural policing, schools, transport, post offices/shops; protect countryside; reform fisheries with regional management; independent Food Commission.
- Urban: regeneration partnerships; community policing; urban road pricing for transit; London strategic authority; participatory planning.

Health and care
- Maintain a comprehensive NHS, free at point of need.
- Six‑month halt to finance‑driven closures pending audit.
- At least £540m extra annually (via closing NI loopholes and +5p per cigarette pack); £200m/year for frontline staff; national pay structure and single review body; cut contracts bureaucracy.
- End two‑tier GP funding; National Inspectorate for Health and Social Care; maximum six‑month wait from diagnosis to treatment over three years.
- Restore free eye and dental checks; freeze prescription charges.
- Strengthen patient rights and local accountability of trusts; improve NHS dentistry access.
- Community care: new Carer’s Benefit; national standards/charging; inspectorate powers; raise care means‑test thresholds as resources allow.

Constitution and governance
- Bill of Rights (ECHR in UK law); Human Rights Commission; Ministry for Justice; Freedom of Information Act; curb quangos; referendums on major constitutional changes.
- Commons reform; reduce MPs by ~200; stricter conduct rules; elected second chamber over two parliaments; proportional representation for all elections; fixed four‑year terms; party finance transparency and caps.
- Devolved legislatures for Scotland and Wales with tax‑varying powers; elected regional assemblies in England where demanded; stronger, more fiscally autonomous local government; long‑term Local Income Tax and reformed business rates.

Equality, welfare and families
- Benefit Transfer Programme for long‑term unemployed; raise tax thresholds (about 500,000 out of tax), funded by a new 50% rate over £100k; replace Income Support/Family Credit with a Low Income Benefit; childcare strategy; voluntary Citizens Service; regionally variable minimum wage; tackle fraud and tax evasion.
- Pensions: earnings‑linked top‑up for low‑income pensioners; flexible retirement 60–70; move towards citizenship‑based pensions; replace SERPS with portable personal/occupational schemes; protect accrued rights; abolish water standing charges.
- Youth: restore benefits for 16–17s; statutory youth service; citizenship/parenting classes.
- Families: parental leave; flexible parental benefit; replace CSA with unified family courts; support adoption/fostering based on suitability; flexible working rights.
- Women: pro‑rata rights for part‑timers; enforce equal pay; pension splitting on divorce; improve NHS access to female professionals; stronger protections against domestic and sexual violence; targets for women on public bodies.
- Disabled people: civil rights law; Partial Capacity Benefit; accessibility codes; accessible public information; enforce SEN code.
- Ethnic minorities: merged equality bodies; statutory employment code; non‑discriminatory immigration and family reunion; restore asylum support; improve policing and sentencing for racist crimes.
- LGBT: equal age of consent; ban discrimination in housing/employment (including armed forces); repeal Section 28; tougher action on homophobic attacks.

Arts, media, digital
- Prevent harmful media concentration; protect BBC independence and licence fee.
- Universal public access to nationwide interactive networks by 2000.
- Lottery to widen arts access; restore free entry for school parties; support film, cultural diplomacy, and BBC World Service.

Foreign policy, defence, development, trade
- Active EU role; more accountable EU institutions; PR for UK MEPs by 1999; wider qualified majority voting with key vetoes retained; “double majority” use; support single currency entry subject to criteria and referendum.
- Strengthen EU foreign/security cooperation; cross‑border crime cooperation with accountability; reform CAP and fisheries (regional management).
- Maintain defence capability; retain Trident with reduced warheads; support NATO enlargement; pursue CTBT and non‑proliferation.
- UN reform: stronger peacekeeping capacity, on‑call forces, Military Staff Committee, UN Staff College; support International Criminal Court.
- Lead on global environmental agreements; create global environmental governance; “environmental Geneva Convention.”
- Development: timetable to 0.7% ODA/GNP within 10 years; untie and target aid; human‑rights conditionality; debt relief.
- Arms control: end sales to human‑rights abusers; tighter EU/UN controls; ban landmines.
- Trade: further reduce barriers (esp. for poorest); labour standards via ILO; environmental clause in GATT; global competition policy.

Judge whether TEXT_E or TEXT_D aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.

  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_E" | "TEXT_D"
}
